newsitem.title: UK: Romania central banker sees 35 pct inflation in 96.
newsitem.headline: Romania central banker sees 35 pct inflation in 96.

text.p: Romania's central bank governor Mugur Isarescu expects year-on-year inflation to be 35 percent by the end of 1996, compared with an IMF-inspired target of 20 percent this year and 33.4 percent in 1995.

"Our preliminary figure for September shows 2.3 percent inflation in that month, so 35 percent for the year will be achievable," Isarescu told Reuters in an interview after the signing of a $175 million syndicated loan arranged by Citibank and ABN Amro in London.

The central banker said that the Romanian leu should trade down from its current level of 3,300 to the dollar to 3,400/3,500. A leading banker in Romania said in a newspaper on Tuesday that its true value was 5,500/6,000.

He said the recent rise in the price of oil would not affect either the current year's inflation level, or foreign exchange reserves and the currency, as most oil for this year had already been contracted.
"We may see inflation carrying on in to next year," Isarescu said.
